name: Air Force waist-to-height ratio

source.document: AFMAN 36-2905, Air Force Physical Fitness Readiness Program (paragraphs 3.1, 3.7 and 3.15.4, Table 3.2)

ifOver: A ratio above 0.55 is high risk. If the whole assessment also falls short (a composite score under 75 or a missed component minimum), a body fat assessment follows (a BIA scale, or a 2-3 site tape measurement): the result must be below 26% for men and below 36% for women, or the assessment is unsatisfactory.
notes: The ratio is cut off (not rounded) after two decimals, so 0.5486 counts as 0.54.
Body composition earns up to 20 points of the Air Force composite score and has no minimum of its own.
The waist is measured three times; the three closest values are averaged and rounded down to 1/2 inch. The standard is the same for every age and sex.
